TITLE: Female Enrollment, Child Mortality and Corruption Are Good Predictors of a Country’s UN Education Index.
FULL_TEXT_REASON: Non-nested feature selection and optimistically biased cross-validation
ASSESSMENT_NOTES: The study analyzes 165 countries and 47 candidate predictors averaged over 2012-2017. Predictors were first filtered using full-sample univariate R-squared values and missingness thresholds. LASSO was then applied using the complete sample, and leave-one-out cross-validation was applied only after the final variables had been selected. Because filtering and LASSO selection were not repeated inside each training fold, the reported out-of-sample R-squared of 0.8936 is exposed to selection leakage and optimistic bias. Three countries were removed because of missing GNI data. No imputation strategy, nested cross-validation, simple baseline, bootstrap selection stability analysis, or reproducible code repository was identified. The article is useful for discussing indicator selection and validation limitations, but its predictive result should not be compared directly with externally grouped validation.
